title: Make a small layer
summary: A layer is a group of units that work on the same incoming values. Two units can produce two outputs from one input.
introduction: A layer is a group of units that work on the same incoming values. Two units can produce two outputs from one input. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A layer is a group of units that work on the same incoming values. Two units can produce two outputs from one input.

blocks.code:
x = 3
first = max(0, x * 2 + 1)
second = max(0, x * -1 + 1)
print([first, second])
blocks.title: Make a small layer

blocks.text: The output is [7, 0]. The first weighted sum is 7. The second is -2, so ReLU changes it to 0.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Use x equal to 0 and calculate both outputs.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Two output values do not mean two examples; here one example produced two values.
